reason: The facts check out, but the REVISED verdict and its recommendation do not. (a) TRUE: exp70b > #37 on the public embryo, unrounded. The UP test is sound (PC16-01 recomputed it: the 6 passed teams kept their SubmissionCount and LastSubmissionDate, and an exact tie cannot produce an UP under earlier-submit tie-breaking). Feasibility is fine. It is a re-tick only: 56592350 is COMPLETE, the ledger gives L (7.41, 7.58] h and 'insertion gate 8.0 h did NOT fire', runtime is proven on the full hidden test, no file is byte-identical, and R8 does not apply. (b) OVERCLAIM: 'weakly dominates' is false by the finding's own numbers, since it gives P(delta<0) 0.08-0.15. At most this is a small expected-value lean. My arithmetic: the public read removes ~7 forks, ~0.4 of them evaluable (R15DS-9). Private is ~2.4x larger, so about 1 evaluable fork is removed there, and P(no private change) is ~0.37. The posterior P(TP | removed evaluable) is ~0.15-0.2. That gives P(<0) ~0.1-0.2, P(>0) ~0.4-0.5 and E ~ +1e-4. (c) POST-HOC, NOT NEW EVIDENCE: R13-A1 (3) limited the 0.954-UP extension to exp70a on purpose ('Class B variants still need a real display >= 0.955'). The reason was that fm45's lab evidence failed on power (T9/L3 FAIL). Points (2) and (4) of the finding reuse that same lab evidence. The only new input is the one-embryo public UP, which is exactly what the rule said not to over-trust; dc0.30 has already shown a lab/public sign flip. The 'lowrefine 4 TP is a bound' point is correct (results.md: lowdet_adverse=true), but it only fixes R16AP-2's wording. It is not new support. (d) DUPLICATE ACTION: D2 (07:41Z) already put '{exp70b, #38} as the public-aimed final' to the user in the ~07:45Z brief (default: no change), and round 16 already has the answer card R16AP-2. The only change here is 'recommend yes' instead of 'neutral'. (e) GAP: the finding ignores the E10 port rule {PORT, #37} ('never drop #37'). A yes on exp70b needs the R16AP-6 slot-table reading ('#37' = the insertion final currently ticked). The old verdict stands: no pre-registered route exists, and a swap is the user's post-hoc call.
